findings.claim: The MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer copies HashCollisionResistant from copyFrom. Any derived instance (WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth, or a subclass copy) silently loses the hash-collision-resistant setting. A security instance created via UntrustedData and then cloned would deserialize Dictionary/HashSet keys with the default non-resistant comparer, which reopens the hash-flooding DoS that MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData is meant to prevent. The change is unrelated to the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test: var s = MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(10); Assert.True(s.HashCollisionResistant). It passes on base and fails on head. Also check that GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer returns the randomized comparer rather than EqualityComparer<T>.Default for the cloned instance, and that a mutant restoring the removed line is killed by this test.
